skill_unlocked.longDescription: Creating your first skill marks your entry into Claude Code's powerful extensibility system. Skills are reusable packages of expertise that Claude can invoke on demand, encapsulating specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools. Unlike simple instructions in CLAUDE.md, skills are modular units that can be triggered by specific contexts or commands, making them ideal for complex, repeatable tasks.
skill_unlocked.whyItMatters: Skills transform Claude from a general assistant into a specialized expert for your specific domains. They're the foundation for building a personalized AI toolkit.

howTo.summary: Create a SKILL.md file in the skills directory with frontmatter defining the skill's name, description, and optional triggers.

steps.instruction: Create the skills directory structure

code.content: mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/my-first-skill

steps.instruction: Create the SKILL.md file with required frontmatter

code.content:
---
name: My First Skill
description: A helpful skill that does something specific
---

# My First Skill

This skill helps with [specific task].

## When to Use

Use this skill when you need to:
- Handle a specific type of task
- Follow a particular workflow
- Apply specialized knowledge

## Instructions

1. First, do this
2. Then, do that
3. Finally, complete with this

steps.instruction: Test your skill by invoking it in Claude Code
steps.note: Restart Claude Code after creating new skills for them to be detected

description: Systematic code review following best practices

- [ ] Code correctness and logic
- [ ] Error handling completeness

Test skills in real scenarios before relying on them

triggered_skill.longDescription: Triggered skills automatically activate when specific conditions are met, such as when certain file types are opened or specific commands are run. By defining trigger conditions in your skill's frontmatter, you create context-aware assistance that appears exactly when needed without requiring manual invocation. This transforms skills from passive knowledge into active, intelligent helpers.
triggered_skill.whyItMatters: Triggers make skills proactive rather than reactive. Claude automatically knows when your specialized expertise applies, reducing cognitive load and ensuring consistent application of best practices.

howTo.summary: Add a trigger field to your skill's frontmatter that describes when the skill should automatically activate.

steps.instruction: Open your existing skill or create a new one

team_skill.longDescription: Project-level skills live in your repository's .claude/skills directory and are shared with everyone who works on the project. Unlike user-level skills in ~/.claude, team skills travel with the codebase via version control, ensuring consistent AI assistance across your entire team. This is essential for encoding project-specific knowledge, coding standards, and workflows that everyone should follow.
team_skill.whyItMatters: Team skills create a shared foundation of AI-assisted expertise. New team members immediately benefit from encoded project knowledge, and standards are applied consistently regardless of who's working.

howTo.summary: Create skills in ./.claude/skills instead of ~/.claude/skills so they're tracked by git and shared with the team.

steps.instruction: Create the project-level skills directory

steps.instruction: Create a skill encoding project-specific knowledge

code.content:
---
name: Project Standards
description: Coding standards and patterns for this project
---

# Project Standards

## Architecture

- Use the repository pattern for data access
- Services go in /src/services
- Shared utilities in /src/lib

## Naming Conventions

- Components: PascalCase (UserProfile.tsx)
- Utilities: camelCase (formatDate.ts)
- Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE

## Required Patterns

- All API calls go through the api client
- Use Zod for runtime validation
- Error boundaries on page components

reference_writer.longDescription: A reference.md file serves as the comprehensive documentation for your skill, containing detailed specifications, API references, configuration options, and technical details. While examples.md shows how to use the skill, reference.md explains all available options, parameters, and behaviors. This is particularly valuable for complex skills with many configuration possibilities.
reference_writer.whyItMatters: Complete reference documentation ensures Claude has access to every detail needed for accurate, comprehensive assistance. It prevents gaps in knowledge that could lead to incorrect or incomplete outputs.

howTo.summary: Create a reference.md file that documents all options, configurations, and technical details of your skill.

steps.instruction: Create the reference.md file in your skill directory

code.content:
# Reference

## Configuration Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| format | string | 'standard' | Output format style |
| strict | boolean | false | Enable strict mode validation |
| indent | number | 2 | Spaces for indentation |

## Supported Patterns

### Pattern A: Service Layer
- Use when: Business logic needs isolation
- Structure: `/services/{name}Service.ts`
- Required exports: `create`, `update`, `delete`, `getById`

### Pattern B: Repository Layer
- Use when: Database abstraction needed
- Structure: `/repositories/{name}Repository.ts`
- Required methods: CRUD + custom queries

## Error Codes

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
|------|---------|------------|
| E001 | Invalid input | Check schema requirements |
| E002 | Not found | Verify resource exists |
| E003 | Unauthorized | Check permissions |

steps.instruction: Organize reference by topic for easy navigation
steps.note: Use tables, code blocks, and clear headings for scannability

examples.title: CLI Tool Reference

code.content:
# CLI Generator Reference

## Command Structure

```
command <action> [target] [--options]
```

## Actions

### `create`
Creates a new resource.

**Arguments:**
- `target` (required): Resource type to create

**Options:**
- `--template, -t`: Template to use (default: 'basic')
- `--force, -f`: Overwrite existing files
- `--dry-run`: Preview without writing

### `list`
Lists existing resources.

**Options:**
- `--format`: Output format (json|table|plain)
- `--filter`: Filter expression

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|----------|---------|--------|
| CLI_HOME | Config directory | ~/.cli |
| CLI_DEBUG | Enable debug output | false |

These scripts can perform validations, transformations, API calls, or any computation that enhances the skill's capabilities. Scripts turn skills from static knowledge into dynamic, actionable tools that can interact with your system and external services.

examples.title: Code Quality Check Script
examples.description: Script that runs linting and formatting checks

code.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Run code quality checks and report results

set -e

echo "Running code quality checks..."

# TypeScript check
if [ -f "tsconfig.json" ]; then
  echo "Checking TypeScript..."
  npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 || echo "TypeScript errors found"
fi

# Linting
if [ -f ".eslintrc.json" ] || [ -f ".eslintrc.js" ]; then
  echo "Running ESLint..."
  npx eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx --format json 2>&1
fi

# Formatting check
if [ -f ".prettierrc" ]; then
  echo "Checking formatting..."
  npx prettier --check . 2>&1 || echo "Formatting issues found"
fi

echo "Quality check complete"

examples.explanation: This script provides actionable quality feedback that Claude can interpret

error_recovery_skill.longDescription: Skills that define error handling behavior provide graceful degradation when things go wrong. By documenting common errors, fallback strategies, and recovery procedures, you create resilient skills that can handle unexpected situations without failing completely. This includes retry logic, alternative approaches, and clear error messaging that helps users understand and resolve issues.
error_recovery_skill.whyItMatters: Real-world usage encounters errors. Skills with built-in recovery are more reliable and trustworthy. Users can confidently invoke them knowing issues will be handled gracefully rather than causing cascading failures.

howTo.summary: Add error handling documentation to your skill that covers common failures, recovery strategies, and fallback behaviors.

steps.instruction: Identify potential failure points in your skill
steps.note: Consider: missing files, network issues, invalid input, permission errors

steps.instruction: Document error handling in your SKILL.md

code.content:
---
name: API Integration Helper
description: Helps integrate with external APIs
---

# API Integration Helper

## Error Handling

### Network Failures

**If API is unreachable:**
1. Retry with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s)
2. After 3 failures, suggest checking network
3. Offer to use cached data if available

### Authentication Errors

**If credentials are invalid:**
1. Prompt user to verify API key
2. Check if key is in environment variables
3. Guide through credential setup

### Rate Limiting

**If rate limited:**
1. Respect Retry-After header
2. Queue remaining requests
3. Notify user of delay

### Fallback Behavior

When errors persist:
- Use mock data for development
- Provide manual instructions as alternative
- Log error details for debugging

steps.instruction: Include error recovery in your examples

code.content:
## Error Recovery Example

**Scenario:** API returns 503

**Response:**
```
The API is temporarily unavailable. Attempting recovery:

1. Waiting 2 seconds before retry... [retry 1/3]
2. Still unavailable. Waiting 4 seconds... [retry 2/3]
3. Service restored. Proceeding with request.

Alternatively, you can:
- Use offline mode with cached data
- Check API status at status.api.com
- Proceed with mock data for development
```

examples.title: File Processing Error Recovery

code.content:
---
name: File Processor
description: Processes and transforms files with error recovery
---

# File Processor

## Error Recovery

### File Not Found

**Recovery steps:**
1. Check for typos in filename
2. Search for similar files with Glob
3. Suggest creating the file if appropriate

### Permission Denied

**Recovery steps:**
1. Explain the permission issue
2. Suggest running with elevated permissions
3. Offer to write to alternative location

### Invalid Format

**Recovery steps:**
1. Attempt format detection
2. Try common format parsers
3. Ask user to specify format
4. Provide manual parsing guidance

### Partial Failure

**Recovery steps:**
1. Save progress to temp file
2. Report which items succeeded/failed
3. Offer to retry failed items only

tips: Anticipate errors before they happen
Provide actionable recovery suggestions
Never leave users stuck without options
Log detailed error information for debugging

- Default connection: Use DATABASE_URL environment variable
- Prefer safe operations (dry-run by default)
- Always create backups before destructive operations

## Available Commands

- `/db:migrate` - Run database migrations
- `/db:seed` - Seed database with test data
- `/db:backup` - Create database backup
- `/db:restore` - Restore from backup

skill_chain.longDescription: A skill that references or invokes another skill creates a chain of specialized capabilities. By calling /other-skill: within your skill's instructions, you can compose complex workflows from simpler building blocks. This enables sophisticated multi-step processes where each skill handles its area of expertise, passing results along the chain.
skill_chain.whyItMatters: Skill chaining enables composition without duplication. Instead of rebuilding capabilities, you combine existing skills into powerful workflows. This creates a modular ecosystem where skills can be improved independently.

howTo.summary: Reference another skill using its slash command syntax within your skill's instructions.

steps.instruction: Identify skills that complement each other
steps.note: Example: code-review skill + security-check skill = comprehensive review

steps.instruction: Create a skill that chains to others

code.content:
---
name: Full Review Pipeline
description: Comprehensive code review combining multiple checks
---

# Full Review Pipeline

This skill orchestrates a complete code review by chaining specialized skills.

## Review Steps

1. **Code Quality** - Invoke /code-review: for structural analysis
2. **Security Scan** - Chain to /security-check: for vulnerability detection
3. **Performance** - Use /perf-analysis: for performance review
4. **Documentation** - Apply /docs-check: for documentation coverage

## Workflow

When invoked:

1. Run `/code-review:` on the target code
2. Pass findings to `/security-check:` for security context
3. Run `/perf-analysis:` with the code patterns identified
4. Finally, run `/docs-check:` to verify documentation

## Combined Report

Aggregate findings into a single comprehensive report with:
- Critical issues (must fix)
- Security concerns
- Performance suggestions
- Documentation gaps

## Pipeline Stages

### 1. Pre-flight Checks

### 2. Security Gate

```
Chain to /security-scan: for:
```

versioned_skill.whyItMatters: Versioning creates clarity about skill evolution. Teams can pin to specific versions, users know when updates might affect their workflows, and you can maintain multiple versions for different compatibility needs.

skill_updater.longDescription: Updating an installed skill pulls the latest changes from its source, bringing new features, bug fixes, and improvements. For skills installed via git, this is as simple as git pull. Keeping skills updated ensures you have the latest capabilities and security patches while maintaining compatibility with evolving Claude Code features.
skill_updater.whyItMatters: Outdated skills may have bugs, security issues, or miss new features. Regular updates keep your AI toolkit current and reliable, just like updating any other software dependency.

howTo.summary: Update a git-installed skill by pulling the latest changes from its repository.

steps.instruction: Navigate to the skill directory

code.content: cd ~/.claude/skills/skill-name

steps.instruction: Check for available updates

code.content:
git fetch origin
git log HEAD..origin/main --oneline

steps.instruction: Pull the updates

code.content: git pull origin main

steps.instruction: Review the changelog if available

code.content: cat CHANGELOG.md | head -50

steps.instruction: Restart Claude Code to load updates

examples.title: Update All Skills
examples.description: Batch update script for all installed skills

code.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Update all git-based skills

for skill in ~/.claude/skills/*/; do
  if [ -d "$skill/.git" ]; then
    echo "Updating $(basename $skill)..."
    cd "$skill"
    git pull --quiet origin main 2>/dev/null || echo "  (no updates)"
    cd - > /dev/null
  fi
done

echo "All skills updated. Restart Claude Code to apply changes."

examples.explanation: Automate updates for all git-managed skills

code.content:

# Reapply local changes

# Resolve any conflicts if needed
